pairs.subject: data-access
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/db/jobs.ts:980 getJob returns the same null for a job whose payload_json will not decode as for a job that does not exist, so a by-id caller cannot tell 'unreadable' from 'not found'. The decode failure is recorded in the row-issue ledger, but the caller never sees it.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/db/jobs.ts:980 The single-record read folds a decode failure into the not-found answer. The technique says a by-id read of an unreadable record must fail loudly. The mappers are centralised (rowToDevCase etc. via safeRowParse, which logs), so list reads skip bad rows with a record rather than silently.

app/_lib/db/jobs.ts:615 Sort identifiers come from a closed map, sort direction is a two-way ternary, and every value is bound through @named or ? parameters. One soft spot: an unknown sort token falls back to the default order instead of raising a hard error naming the token.
app/_lib/db/jobs.ts:230 Read→compute→write invariants inside one repository operation open their own IMMEDIATE transaction in the layer, and the caller never sees the boundary.

app/_lib/db/devcase.ts:952 A set-shaped read, chunked under the IN limit, that returns a keyed Map so a missing key is explicit. getJobsByIds (jobs.ts:1047) is also chunked but returns a filtered list in input order rather than a map.
app/_lib/db/jobs.ts:287 The list read selects a preview projection instead of loading full JD bodies. devcase.ts:1039 has another status-only projection that skips the JSON parse.
app/_lib/db/jobs.ts:643 The mandatory tenant predicate is inlined in every statement, and a source-guard test asserts it is present. That is the weakest structural form the technique accepts.
app/_lib/db/devcase-publish-dedup.test.ts:20 Tests run against the real better-sqlite3 engine on a throwaway file, with the schema built by the production ensureDb() path.

pairs.registryProposal: The existence-authority-written-last delete rule (remove the authority first) conflicts with erasure deletes. interviews.ts:1008 deliberately unlinks the recording file BEFORE marking the row deleted, so a crash never leaves a row claiming a deletion that did not happen. The technique should name this inversion: when the row is the deletion receipt rather than the existence proof, the order flips.
